## 5. A finite experiment with a predetermined repetition count

An asymptotic exponent advantage does not by itself specify when a finite experiment exhibits the advantage. I resolved that operation separately.

For a faithful swap-balanced output pair \(A,B\), let

\[
x=\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt A\sqrt B.
\]

The new finite-copy bound is

\[
\boxed{
\frac{x^n}{4}
\exp\!\left[-\sqrt n\,\operatorname{arcosh}(1/x)\right]
\le e_n(A,B)
\le\frac{x^n}{2}.
}
\]

Here \(e_n\) is the optimal equal-prior error after \(n\) independent copies.

The proof uses the Nussbaum–Szkoła classical distributions associated with the two quantum states. Swap balance makes the tilted log-likelihood have mean zero. Its exponential moment controls its variance through

\[
\mathbb E\cosh(L/2)=1/x,
\qquad
\mathbb E L^2
\le4\operatorname{arcosh}(1/x)^2.
\]

The finite quantum/classical comparison then gives the lower bound. The upper bound is the half-order quantum Chernoff inequality. Those two imported inequalities are taken from the original primary papers; the displayed dimension-independent conversion is derived in the report. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"}

Suppose the two detectors’ affinities satisfy

\[
x_P-x_Q\ge\varepsilon>0.
\]

Define

\[
b_\varepsilon
=
\min\{b\in\mathbb N:2^b\varepsilon\ge2\},
\qquad
n_\varepsilon
=
\left\lceil\frac{8b_\varepsilon^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right\rceil.
\]

Then, for every \(n\ge n_\varepsilon\),

\[
\boxed{e_n(Q)<\frac1{16}e_n(P).}
\]

There is also an explicit absolute gap:

\[
e_n(P)-e_n(Q)

\Gamma_n
:=
\frac{15}{64}\,
\varepsilon^n
2^{-b_\varepsilon\lceil\sqrt n\rceil}.
\]

Thus the positive witness has a finite operational consequence with a repetition count computed before the reference witness is found.

The exact compiler stores quantities such as \(\varepsilon^n\) as factored rational expressions. This is essential because the guaranteed counts can be enormous. ## 6. Robustness and actual implementations

The obstruction survives specified perturbations of valid detectors.

If corresponding effects satisfy

\[
(1-\delta)E_i
\le E_i'
\le(1+\delta)E_i,
\qquad 0\le\delta<1,
\]

then, for either benchmark,

\[
\boxed{
|V(P',Q')-V(P,Q)|
\le
\log_2\frac{1+\delta}{1-\delta}.
}
\]

At \(\delta=1/16\), this is less than \(1/5\) bit. The compiled zero-versus-one family therefore retains a less-than-\(1/5\) versus greater-than-\(4/5\) separation in computably specified neighborhoods of valid detectors. Additive-\(1/4\) outputs still separate those neighborhoods.

For \(k\) independent primitive implementations, a sufficient relative effect tolerance is

\[
\delta_{\mathrm{base}}=\frac1{16k}.
\]

The independence condition matters: a one-call calibration certificate does not control arbitrary correlated memory errors across repetitions.

Preparation tolerances are explicit as well. An affinity gap \(\varepsilon\) survives at least as \(\varepsilon/2\) if each underlying hypothesis has trace-norm preparation error at most

\[
t\le(\varepsilon/16)^2
\]

and each detector has relative effect error at most \(\varepsilon/8\). Applying the exact fair-bit swap to the prepared underlying pair preserves the symmetry required by the finite-copy bound. The predetermined count becomes \(n_{\varepsilon/2}\).

I also constructed a guarantee for a **specified compiled decision test**, beyond a statement about the optimum. With tighter tolerances

\[
t,\delta_P,\delta_Q\le\frac{\Gamma_n}{16n},
\qquad
\|T_E'-T_E\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\frac{\Gamma_n}{16},
\]

and nominal compilation error at most \(\Gamma_n/16\), the implemented \(Q\) test beats even the actual optimal \(P\) test by more than \(3\Gamma_n/4\).

This uses objective-value approximation of the binary test. It requires neither a spectral gap in the Helstrom operator nor a continuous choice of its exact spectral projector.

The detector’s physical complement is also explicit. For every POVM,

\[
V_E|\psi\rangle
=
\sum_i
|i\rangle_B|i\rangle_F\sqrt{E_i}|\psi\rangle_G
\]

is an isometry, and its actual complementary channel is

\[
E^c(X)=\bigoplus_i\sqrt{E_i}X\sqrt{E_i}.
\]

The experiment discards that environment and retains the stated reference locally. No helper transmission channel is implicit.

7. What this adds, and what remains distinct

A source comparison established that Astra N676 already contains the qualitative Petz/Chernoff order equivalence, the balancing operation, and the quadratic endpoint classification. Those are prior results, and the report attributes them explicitly to the 
pinned governing source.

The additions established here are:

An explicit faithful source-to-affinity conversion with an absolute margin independent of the unknown reference dimension.
Fixed-additive-accuracy impossibility for the two specified discrimination benchmarks.
An implemented algebraic finite-reference optimizer and the resulting impossibility of computing approximately sufficient reference memory.
A dimension-independent finite-copy conversion with predetermined repetition counts.
Calibration, preparation, and compiled-test robustness with stated physical costs.

The comparison with current primary research preserves its actual operational settings. The generalized Chernoff theorem treats composite hypotheses drawn from convex tensor-stable sets; the present experiment uses fixed-pair independent copies. Hirche’s current estimation work supplies related coherent-reference and channel-order machinery. Neither substitutes for the quantitative margin constructed here. 
arxiv.org
+1

Likewise, the 2026 capacity paper proves ordinary-capacity QMA hardness using circuit descriptions, while its undecidability result concerns a restricted entanglement-assisted one-shot zero-error classical capacity. Those results do not resolve ordinary unassisted quantum-capacity approximation, and neither does this continuation. 
arxiv.org

The new principle is precise: finite quantum decision problems can have computable optima at every specified memory size, computable repetition and precision requirements for positive witnesses, yet no computable memory budget guaranteeing even a coarse approximation to their unrestricted optimum. The construction identifies the resource carrying that obstruction and proves that its useful size cannot be universally bounded by an algorithm.
